text: If you smell gas, chemicals or see unusual smoke from Jebel Ali Port or the Free Zone, move away immediately.
Move crosswind or upwind of the plume; never walk downwind of smoke.
Go indoors quickly and shut all windows, doors and balcony doors.
Turn off AC, fans and ventilation that draw outside air.
Seal door gaps and vents with wet towels or tape.
Shelter in an interior room above ground floor for most light gases; avoid basements for heavy gases.
Do not use lifts if the building may be affected; use stairs.
Do not light flames, smoke or switch on sparks if a gas leak is suspected.
Wet a cloth and hold over nose and mouth if smoke enters; breathe through it.
If chemicals contact skin, remove contaminated clothing and rinse with water for 15 minutes.
Do not induce vomiting after swallowing a chemical; call 998 or 997.
Rinse eyes with clean water for at least 15 minutes; remove contact lenses.
Keep pets indoors and bring them into the shelter room.
Wait for official all-clear before opening windows or leaving.
Ventilate the home fully after the all-clear.
Throw away exposed open food; wash sealed containers before use.
Keep a battery radio or charged phone to follow official updates.
Tell Civil Defence (997) the colour, smell and direction of any visible plume.
Do not drive toward the incident; keep roads clear for emergency vehicles.
Learn the hazard sign colours on trucks near the port; report leaking containers to 997.
On a siren or alert, move at once to the most interior room, away from windows.
Stay away from glass, mirrors and heavy hanging items.
Lower floors of a sturdy building are safer than top floors; avoid the roof and balcony.
Do not film or watch from windows or balconies.
Drop to the floor, cover head and neck with arms, and stay down during a blast.
Open your mouth slightly to reduce pressure injury if an explosion is close.
Stay sheltered at least 30 minutes after the last blast unless officials say otherwise.
Expect secondary blasts; do not rush outside.
If driving, stop away from bridges, tunnels and buildings; get low beside the car or enter a sturdy building.
If outdoors with no cover, lie flat in a low spot and cover your head.
After a blast, check yourself and others for injuries before moving.
Control heavy bleeding with firm direct pressure using clean cloth.
Do not touch unexploded objects or debris; stay back and call 999.
Avoid damaged buildings; check for gas smell and exposed wires.
Turn off gas and electricity at the main only if safe to do so.
Use text messages rather than calls to keep phone lines free.
Keep a torch, not candles, for light.
Do not spread unverified videos or rumours; rely on official sources.
Keep shoes beside your bed to protect feet from broken glass.
Agree a household meeting point and plan before any alert.
Learn two exit routes from your apartment and building before an emergency.
Count the doors between your door and the nearest stairwell so you can find it in smoke.
Never use lifts during a fire or evacuation; use the stairs.
Touch doors with the back of your hand; do not open a hot door.
Stay low under smoke where the air is cleaner.
Close doors behind you to slow fire and smoke.
Walk down on the right side and leave the left free for responders.
Help children, elderly and disabled neighbours if you can do so safely.
If trapped, seal door gaps with wet cloth and signal from a window; call 997 with your exact flat number.
Discovery Gardens buildings are low and mid-rise; know your building and zone name.
Do not jump; wait for rescue if you cannot exit.
Take phone, keys, ID and meds only if it costs no time.
Gather at the building assembly point and report to a warden or responders.
Do not re-enter until Civil Defence says it is safe.
Test your smoke alarm monthly and keep a fire extinguisher accessible.
Keep corridors, stairwells and balcony exits clear of belongings.
Know where your building's fire panel and extinguishers are.
Keep a small grab bag by the door with documents, cash and meds.
Photograph key documents and keep copies in cloud storage and on your phone.
Tell your building management about residents who need evacuation help.
Store at least 3 litres of drinking water per person per day for at least 3 days; 7 days is better.
Keep water in sealed bottles in a cool, dark place and rotate every 6 months.
Fill bathtub or clean containers if you expect supply cuts.
Boil water for 1 minute if its safety is doubtful, or use purification tablets.
Stock non-perishable food: canned fish and beans, rice, dates, nuts, biscuits.
Buy a manual can opener and ready-to-eat items that need no cooking.
Keep a 7-day supply of regular medicines and a basic first-aid kit.
Include infant formula, nappies and pet food if relevant.
Keep power banks charged and a car charger available.
Store a torch, spare batteries and a battery or crank radio.
Keep small cash in AED, since card systems and ATMs may fail.
Keep your car at least half full of fuel.
Do not panic-buy beyond your needs; leave supplies for others.
Eat perishable food first when power fails; keep the fridge closed.
Use bottled water for drinking and cooking only; save other water for hygiene.
Pack a grab bag: water, snacks, meds, documents, charger, whistle.
Keep hygiene supplies: wipes, soap, hand sanitiser, tissue and bin bags.
Know ramadan or religious dietary needs when preparing supplies.
Store supplies off the floor and away from heat and sunlight.
Check expiry dates every 3 months and replace as needed.
Emergency numbers in Dubai: Police 999, Civil Defence 997, Ambulance 998.
Dubai Police non-emergency line is 901.
DEWA (power and water) emergency line is 991.
Register with your embassy or consulate in the UAE and save its 24-hour number offline.
Use the Embassy Locator button to find your embassy or consulate on the map.
Most consulates are in Dubai or Abu Dhabi; check your country's travel advisory page.
Keep passport, Emirates ID and visa copies in a waterproof pouch and on your phone.
Keep at least 6 months passport validity if you may need to travel.
Save contact numbers of an out-of-country family member as your message relay.
Follow NCEMA, Dubai Police and Dubai Media Office official accounts for verified updates.
Enable government emergency alerts on your phone settings.
Download the Dubai Police app and the UAE official alert apps and test them now.
Check airline and Dubai Airports updates before travelling; airspace may close at short notice.
Know your employer's emergency contact and HR duty line.
Tell your landlord or building management your emergency contact details.
Keep a printed card with blood type, allergies and medicines for each family member.
Use the I'm Safe button to log check-ins and share them by SMS.
If you are a foreign resident, keep your sponsor and company contact numbers handy.
Do not post sensitive locations or incidents on social media.
Verify news with at least two official sources before acting or forwarding.
Learn basic first aid: control bleeding, CPR, recovery position.
Call 998 for medical emergencies and give your exact location and landmark.
Keep a tourniquet or strong bandage and gauze in your first-aid kit.
Stay hydrated; Dubai heat adds risk during any emergency without AC.
Move heat stroke victims to shade and cool them with water and fans.
Keep phone on low power mode and screen brightness low to save battery.
Download offline maps of Jebel Ali and Discovery Gardens in advance.
Send SMS instead of calling to reduce network load.
Agree on a family text code like SAFE or HELP and a rendezvous point.
Write key phone numbers on paper in case the phone dies.
